question:
“Prevention is better than cure”. Researching and treating diseases is too costly so it would be better to invest in prevention measures.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
It is widely argued that preventing the diseases is more vital and important than treatment to have a healthy society. Health is the greatest asset of each nation which government should look after. It is suggested to allocate the state budget to providing prevention strategies rather than treating illnesses. I strongly agree with prevention measures to enrich everybody’s lifestyle as it will greatly benefit both society and individual.

At the society level, a healthy community is characterized by members who adopted a healthy lifestyle. It will lead to less hospital construction or other healthcare institutes. Furthermore, doctors and nurses would not become occupied with fewer proportion of sick people. For instance, Covid-19 has approved that all countries not only developing but also developed ones did not invest vastly on prevention strategies. They are, therefore, dealing with allocating their treasure to invention of a proper vaccine as a cure to save people’s lives.

What’s more, the prevention strategies and free disease detection of tests should become available to public. At the personal level, individuals will save their lives and their money by easy access to free testing or prevention measures. Therefore, the workplaces can become healthier and individuals can spend their money on the other fields rather than treating illnesses, which could lead to an economic prosperity in the long run.

All things considered, health of a nation can be influenced greatly by investing more state budget on prevention strategies. The government ought to prioritize prevention measures rather than disease treatment. Personally, I believe that the expenses of facilitating individuals with prevention strategies and free disease testings will be recouped many times over by having a healthy nation.
